cli_fixed_cost_ms.method: tesseract on a 32x32 blank PNG, n=20, vs ~0.0 ms for the same call through the reused FFI handle

rationale: OCR cost is set by tesseract itself, not by how it is called: all four calling mechanisms land within 15% of each other (crop 277-352 ms, full frame 3.3-4.7 s), and the CLI's removable per-call overhead is a measured 60 ms - 18% of a crop, 1.6% of a full frame. A persistent worker wins on two grounds the FFI-in-process option does not: it removes those 60 ms AND it keeps tesseract's OpenMP runtime out of the main process, which cost a reproducible ~800 ms (20%) per full frame when ctypes-libtesseract shared a process with numpy/OpenBLAS - and it is what the concurrency requirement in DESIGN.md 4.4 needs anyway. Dropping tesseract is not an option: the local VLM (gemma4:26b, vision) is 45x slower on a crop and returns nothing at all on a full frame, because a 7.4 MP screenshot is encoded as ~256 image tokens and the model degenerates into a hallucinated repetition loop.
